chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Uqba, who said:

Abu al-Khattab, before he was spoiled, used to carry the questions to our companions and return with their answers. He reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Buy, even if it is expensive, for sustenance descends with the purchase.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ: Abu al-Kattab, a prominent companion of the Imams known for his role in transmitting hadith before his death.
key_terms.الشِّرَاءِ: The act of purchasing or buying.
key_terms.يَفْسُدَ: Spoiled or died, referring to the end of his life or his transition from this world.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and economic significance of spending money in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Ali ibn Uqba, a prominent companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith highlights the spiritual dimension of economic activity, where the act of purchasing serves as a catalyst for divine sustenance (rizq). It reflects the Shia scholarly view that active engagement in trade, rather than passive hoarding, aligns the believer with the flow of provision, encouraging confidence in God's promise despite market fluctuations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Uqba who said,

‘Abu Al-Khatab, before he was spoil, and he used to carry the questions of our companions, and come back with their answers, (he) reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Buy, even though it may be expensive, as the sustenance descends for the buyer (when he spends)’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn ‘Atiyyah who has said the following:

“Abu al-Khattab (meaning Muhammad ibn Miqlas al-Asadiy al-Kufiy) before destroying his belief would present the legal questions of the members of the community before the Imam and bring back the answers. He has narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, the following: ‘You should purchase goods even if prices are high; sustenance comes by means of buying.’”
